title: Replacing the port crane operators
scenario: Port director Jorge Valverde in Valparaiso has approved a pilot of remotely operated, partly automated cranes. The system would cut accidents and let the port handle more ships, which the regional government wants. Ninety-four crane operators, many second-generation dockworkers, would be offered retraining for fewer remote roles; most would not be needed. Their union has threatened a strike that would stall exports during the harvest season. Jorge can phase the transition over three years or move faster to win a contract with an international shipping line that expires its offer in two months.
options: Move quickly to secure the shipping contract, paying generous severance and funding retraining for every affected operator.
Phase the transition over three years through attrition and retraining, accepting that the shipping line may withdraw its offer.
Delay automation until negotiating a job guarantee with the union, accepting lost business and a possible loss of the port's competitiveness.

title: Autopilot override on the commuter ferry
scenario: Captain Ayesha Rahman pilots a ferry across the Bosphorus, where an automated navigation assistant now handles most manoeuvres. In thick fog, the system steers toward a berth while her own judgement tells her the approach angle is wrong, though she cannot be sure and the system has an excellent record. Two hundred commuters are aboard. If she overrides and is wrong, she will have violated the operator's protocol, which holds her personally responsible for deviations. If she trusts the system and it errs, the collision would be blamed on automation. She has seconds to decide.
options: Override the system and take manual control, trusting her seasoned judgement over the machine in conditions she has handled for years.
Let the system continue but prepare to intervene instantly at the first sign of deviation, accepting the delay in acting.
Abort the approach, circle and request tugboat assistance, accepting delay and an incident report even though the system was probably correct.

title: Who answers when the dosing robot errs
scenario: Pharmacy director Dr. Linh Pham at a Hanoi hospital oversees an automated dispensing robot that prepares chemotherapy doses. A rare labelling error led to a patient receiving a slightly wrong dose, with mild harm. The manufacturer blames the pharmacist who loaded the vials, who followed training; the pharmacist says the robot's interface was confusing; the hospital's insurer wants one responsible party named. Naming the pharmacist would likely end her career, while naming the system could lead to the hospital halting automation that has otherwise prevented many errors. Linh must submit the incident report this week.
options: Attribute the error to a combination of system design and training failings, recommending interface fixes and no individual discipline.
Name the pharmacist's procedural lapse as the proximate cause in line with the manufacturer's account and the insurer's needs.
Suspend the robot until the manufacturer proves the interface fix works, accepting that manual compounding carries its own error rate.
tension: patient safety vs. continuity of a useful tool

title: A bookkeeping tool and the village accountant
scenario: Savita Joshi, an accountant in a small Maharashtra town, has served local shopkeepers for thirty years. A cheap AI bookkeeping app now handles invoices and tax filings for a fraction of her fee. Her clients, mostly elderly, trust her and struggle with apps, but younger shop owners are leaving. Savita could adopt the same tool herself and offer cheaper services, laying off her two assistants, or continue offering personal service at higher prices and risk gradual decline. A relative suggests she sell her client list now to a larger firm. She must decide before the tax season starts in three weeks.
options: Adopt the app, reduce fees, and lay off her two assistants to keep the practice viable in the long term.
Keep the assistants and personal service, accepting lower income and a slow loss of younger clients.
Sell the client list to the larger firm on condition that it retains her assistants for at least a year.
tension: loyalty to employees vs. survival of the business

title: Warehouse robots and the temp agency
scenario: Regional manager Pieter van Rijn at a Dutch distribution centre is planning to introduce picking robots that will reduce the need for temporary agency workers by half. Many agency workers are migrants from Eastern Europe who send wages home and have no contractual claim to continued work. Permanent employees will be offered retraining and are protected. Pieter's headquarters expects a figure for savings by Friday, and any promise to agency workers would have to come from a budget he does not control. He can recommend how the transition should treat people who have no formal status in the plan.
options: Recommend that agency workers be given first priority for retraining slots and a notice period beyond the legal minimum.
Recommend the plan as drafted, since agency contracts are temporary by nature and obligations lie with the permanent workforce.
Recommend slowing the rollout so agency contracts expire naturally over a year, reducing the shock but delaying the savings.

title: Auto-grader for the essay exam
scenario: Chief examiner Dr. Grace Mwangi in Dar es Salaam faces a backlog of three hundred thousand handwritten essays and a shortage of markers, leaving students waiting months for results needed for university entry. An AI marking system can grade within days, with accuracy comparable to human markers on average, though it struggles with essays written in nonstandard Swahili dialects and unconventional structures. Teachers worry the system rewards formulaic writing. Grace must decide how it will be used for this year's national exams, with results due before university applications close.
options: Use the AI for all essays and have human markers review any that score near the pass thresholds.
Use the AI to pre-sort essays and send all those flagged as unusual in language or structure to human markers.
Keep human marking only, extending the results date and accepting that some students will miss university application deadlines.

title: The self-checkout expansion at a family grocery chain
scenario: Owner-operator Rosalind Achterberg of a South African grocery chain wants to install self-checkouts across her stores. Customers prefer shorter queues, and shoplifting is manageable. But eighty cashiers, many of them single mothers who have worked for her for over a decade, would see their hours cut, and the new roles require skills in technology that older staff doubt they have. Competitors are installing the machines and her prices may no longer be competitive. Rosalind has to commit to the contract with the machine supplier by month end to secure the discount.
options: Install self-checkouts in all stores and offer cashiers a paid six-month transition programme for the new roles or severance.
Install them in half the stores and keep traditional lanes elsewhere, accepting reduced savings and a slower response to competitors.
Postpone installation and compete on service, accepting the risk of customers and business moving to rival stores.

title: Teaching assistant bot for the overloaded lecturer
scenario: Dr. Mikael Berg, a lecturer in Uppsala, supervises four hundred students in a first-year course with only two tutors. The university provides an AI teaching assistant that answers students' questions and gives feedback on drafts. In a trial, student satisfaction rose, but the tutors, both doctoral students who depend on the teaching income, would lose hours. The bot occasionally gives confidently wrong explanations. If Mikael uses it fully, the department will praise the cost saving and may cut tutor positions for good. The semester begins soon and he has to arrange the course staffing.
options: Use the bot to handle routine questions and keep both tutors on for in-depth discussion and checking the bot's answers.
Use the bot as the main support channel and reduce the tutors' hours, accepting savings for the department and income loss for the tutors.
Decline to use the bot in the first semester, relying on the tutors until its reliability can be studied further.
tension: student access vs. junior staff livelihoods

title: Translating asylum interviews by machine
scenario: Registrar Collins Oduya at a tribunal in Nairobi must decide whether to use machine translation for hearings involving refugees from Eritrea and South Sudan, where human interpreters are scarce and cases often wait over a year. Machine translation is fast, but the system sometimes mistranslates details of dates and places, which determine credibility in asylum decisions. Human interpreters would have to be hired from a small pool and may have community ties to the applicants. A significant backlog means families remain in limbo. Collins can approve one approach for the next sitting, which starts on Monday.
options: Use machine translation for all hearings, with the recording preserved so disputed passages can be checked by a human later.
Use machine translation for preliminary hearings only, reserving human interpreters for final credibility interviews.
Continue with human interpreters only, hiring additional ones despite their limited numbers and the longer queue.

title: Railway signalling and the retirement of the signalmen
scenario: Rail operations chief Ludmila Horakova in Czechia is planning automatic signalling across a regional line. The system has passed safety tests, but a number of experienced signalmen warn it cannot replicate their intuition for unusual situations, like a late-night herd of animals crossing the tracks or a landslip. The ministry wants the old signal boxes closed to cut costs. Retained staff could remain as supervisors, but only a third of posts are needed. She can set the handover plan, and the first line is due to switch over in a month.
options: Switch over on schedule, retain the most experienced third as remote supervisors, and offer early retirement to the rest.
Run the old and new systems in parallel for a year to test the automatic system under real conditions before closing any signal box.
Close the signal boxes as ministry policy requires, trusting the testing, and invest the savings in the new system's safety monitoring.

title: Selling the robot barista to the founder's friend
scenario: Ahn Seo-yeon manages a cafe chain in Busan and has been approached by a robotics vendor with an offer of automated coffee kiosks. The kiosks would replace twenty part-time baristas, mostly university students who depend on the job for tuition. Her friend, the founder of the vendor, hinted that purchases from early customers get a lasting discount. Customers enjoy conversation with the baristas, but queues are long. The chain's owner left the decision to her and is more focused on the profit figure. She has to reply to the vendor by the end of next week.
options: Buy the kiosks for the busiest stores only, and offer displaced students shifts in other stores wherever available.
Decline the kiosks and promote the human service as the chain's differentiator, accepting slower growth and possibly lower profits.
Buy kiosks for every store and offer the displaced students a one-off scholarship payment funded from the savings.

title: Crop-spraying drones and the day labourers
scenario: Cooperative chair Bartolomeu Lima in northeast Brazil is offered a subsidised fleet of spraying drones for his members' fruit farms. Drones would apply pesticides more precisely, reducing exposure and chemical use, and members have long complained about workers' poisoning. However, it would eliminate seasonal spraying jobs held by landless families in a region with little other work. The subsidy offer expires soon, and members are divided between large and small farms. Bartolomeu must call the cooperative's vote and decide how to present the choice to the members.
options: Present the drones as a safety improvement and propose a fund, financed by savings, to support affected seasonal workers.
Recommend rejecting the subsidy, protecting the jobs while acknowledging the continuing health risk for the workers who stay.
Recommend adopting drones gradually, starting with the most hazardous chemicals and retaining manual spraying for safer treatments.

title: Verdict support for the overworked magistrate
scenario: Magistrate Ioana Dumitrescu in Cluj has more than nine hundred open cases. Her court has introduced software that drafts judgments in routine contract disputes by summarising evidence and suggesting outcomes. She has used it on simple cases and finds it accurate, but a recent draft contained a fabricated citation that she nearly missed. Colleagues who rely on it clear their dockets faster and receive praise from the ministry. Ioana is considering whether to continue reviewing every draft line by line, which slows her down, or to trust the tool for the simplest cases.
options: Continue verifying every citation and every conclusion in every draft, accepting a slower docket and a lower performance ranking.
Use the drafts for routine cases and spot-check a sample, accepting a small risk of undetected error for faster justice.
Use the tool only for summaries of evidence and write all reasoning and outcomes herself, gaining some time but less than colleagues.

title: Autonomous haul trucks at the copper mine
scenario: Mine superintendent Pedro Quispe-Mamani in the Peruvian Andes has been told to deploy driverless haul trucks, which would operate around the clock and reduce fatal accidents that have plagued the site. About a hundred and ten drivers, from nearby highland communities that depend on the mine, would lose their jobs, while about thirty remote operators would be hired, probably from the capital. The community council has asked for a say in the process. The mining company intends to proceed, and Pedro controls the hiring approach for the remote roles.
options: Hire the remote operators from local communities with a funded training programme, accepting a slower start and higher cost.
Hire the most qualified remote operators from anywhere, and fund a separate community development programme in compensation.
Delay deployment until the community council has negotiated terms, accepting that the company may overrule him or replace him.

title: A chatbot takes over the immigration help desk
scenario: Service manager Catarina Silveira runs a municipal help desk in Lisbon for newcomers navigating residence permits. A multilingual chatbot could answer routine questions around the clock and free her five caseworkers for complex cases. Pilot data shows that people with low literacy or no smartphone are the ones most likely to miss deadlines, and the chatbot occasionally gives outdated rules after policy changes. The city wants to cut opening hours of the physical desk as a saving. Catarina has to submit her recommended service model to the council on Thursday.
options: Recommend the chatbot with the physical desk kept open at reduced hours, with priority for those who cannot use the digital channel.
Recommend the chatbot plus a fixed monthly accuracy audit, and move two caseworkers to outreach rather than counter service.
Recommend keeping the existing desk unchanged, rejecting the chatbot until reliability on rule changes can be demonstrated.
tension: access for the digitally excluded vs. service efficiency

title: Radiologist or algorithm, who signs the report
scenario: Senior radiologist Dr. Tendai Moyo in Harare is under pressure from a hospital group to sign off on large batches of chest scans pre-read by an AI system. Her signature carries legal responsibility. The AI is quite accurate but has flagged a few false negatives in testing. Reading each scan fully would mean she can only process about a third of the volume, leaving patients waiting weeks for results in a country with few radiologists. She has been asked to adopt a signing method before next week, and any approach she chooses will set precedent for younger colleagues.
options: Sign batches after reviewing only scans the AI marks abnormal or uncertain, accepting a small risk of missed findings in the rest.
Read every scan herself, accepting long waits for patients and conflict with the hospital group.
Sign batches based on the AI, and arrange for a rotating colleague to re-read a random ten percent as quality control.
tension: throughput vs. legal and moral responsibility
access to care vs. diagnostic certainty

title: The news desk and the summary generator
scenario: Editor-in-chief Mirela Hasani at a Kosovo-based news outlet is offered an AI tool that writes short news items from agency feeds, freeing reporters for original investigations. Four junior journalists who write those items would be reassigned to riskier fieldwork or let go. Past mistakes by the tool included a misattributed quote. The outlet has just lost a major advertiser and may close within a year without cuts. Mirela can adopt the tool, keep things as they are, or propose a compromise to the owner before the budget meeting on Monday.
options: Adopt the tool for agency items with an editor checking every item before publication, and retrain the junior journalists for field reporting.
Keep human writers and cut other costs, such as office space and her own salary, to avoid losing the juniors.
Adopt the tool fully and let go of two junior journalists, using savings to protect the investigative team's work.

title: The pilots' union and single-pilot cockpits
scenario: Airline safety executive Captain Reinhild Vogt is asked to assess a proposal to operate cargo flights with a single pilot supported by an advanced automated co-pilot system. The system has handled thousands of simulated emergencies, but a rare simulated medical incapacitation exposed a gap. The airline's cost savings are large, and cargo flights carry no passengers, though they overfly populated areas. Pilot unions oppose it vehemently. Reinhild's report goes directly to the board, and she must state whether she regards it as acceptably safe, or recommend more testing that could delay the plan by years.
options: Recommend approval limited to routes over unpopulated areas, with the incapacitation gap fixed first.
Recommend further testing across a broader range of scenarios before any single-pilot operation, even at the cost of years of delay.
Recommend approval on the basis of overall simulated safety, which matches or exceeds two-pilot performance in most scenarios.

title: A grandmother's care robot and the paid carer
scenario: Kwabena Boateng in Accra is a daughter-in-law managing the care of her bedridden mother-in-law. A neighbour sells a home care robot that reminds the patient to take medicine, monitors vital signs and alerts family in emergencies, at a cost equal to six months of the wages of Abena, the part-time carer who has looked after the old woman for five years. Abena is attached to her patient and depends on this income for her own children's school fees. Kwabena's husband favours the robot's reliability, and she must decide with him this weekend.
options: Buy the robot and keep Abena employed at reduced hours for companionship and tasks the robot cannot do.
Keep Abena as the sole carer and decline the robot, valuing the human relationship and the loyalty owed to her.
Buy the robot and end Abena's employment with a generous severance and a written reference, accepting the harm to her.
tension: family budget vs. a worker's livelihood

title: Code-writing assistant and the apprentice programmers
scenario: Engineering lead Dilnoza Karimova at a Tashkent software outsourcing company notices that junior developers now use an AI coding assistant for most tasks, producing working code faster but learning less. Senior staff worry that no one will develop the deep skills needed later. The company's profit depends on speed, and clients like cheaper delivery. Banning the assistant would put her team behind competitors; allowing it unreservedly might hollow out the next generation of experts. She must set the team's policy before the new intake of graduates joins in September.
options: Allow the assistant freely for delivery work and run separate training exercises without it to protect skill growth.
Ban the assistant for the first six months of each junior's employment so they learn fundamentals before using it.
Allow it everywhere but require juniors to explain every piece of generated code in review, accepting slower throughput.

title: Autonomous tractors and the farm hand's pension
scenario: Farmer Seamus Mac Cumhaill in County Mayo is considering an autonomous tractor for his hill sheep farm and the lower fields. It would reduce his labour costs and the danger of accidents on slopes, a worry since his neighbour was killed in a rollover. His farm hand, Declan, has worked for him thirty years, is sixty-two, and has no pension beyond the state minimum. Seamus's own income is shrinking and his son has moved to the city. The dealer's offer ends in two weeks, and Seamus does not know how to reconcile his safety, finances and obligations.
options: Buy the tractor and keep Declan on, doing lighter work, until retirement age, accepting the lower financial gain.
Buy the tractor and retire Declan with a settlement funded from the equipment savings, replacing his income as far as possible.
Do not buy the tractor, continuing with existing methods and accepting the safety and cost risks to protect Declan's job.
tension: personal safety vs. loyalty to an employee

title: Credit committee and the loan officer's judgement
scenario: Branch manager Saeed Kakar in Peshawar oversees loan officers who have long relied on personal knowledge of borrowers. The bank's head office wants every loan above a threshold to be decided by an automated system, with officers merely entering data. Officers say they know which traders are trustworthy even if their paperwork is poor. The system would approve more loans faster, but refuse many who lack documents. Saeed's job is to implement the policy but he can set the threshold for local cases within a range, and he must submit his proposal for the new process by Wednesday.
options: Set the threshold high so officers retain discretion over small and medium loans, where paperwork gaps are common.
Set the threshold low to comply fully with head office, and let borrowers unable to meet documentation requirements seek other lenders.
Set the threshold at the middle of the permitted range and let officers attach written recommendations that the system must display to approvers.

title: Driverless shuttle in a retirement community
scenario: Community director Phyllis Okafor-Brandt at a retirement village in Arizona must choose whether to replace the human-driven shuttle with a driverless one. The autonomous shuttle would save money, run more hours, and avoid the cases of tired drivers. Residents are divided. Some love the idea, while others say the driver, Mr. Elkins, is their daily social contact and helps them with bags and appointments. The shuttle cannot assist anyone physically. Phyllis must report to the residents' association on Saturday, and funds saved could pay for extra activities.
options: Adopt the driverless shuttle and hire Mr. Elkins as a paid community companion who greets and assists riders at the main stops.
Keep the human-driven shuttle and treat the social contact it provides as a core part of the community's service.
Run the driverless shuttle on fixed routes and keep the human-driven one by reservation for residents needing assistance.
tension: cost and capability vs. human contact
one worker's role vs. community benefit

title: Algorithmic trading desk and the departing trader
scenario: Head of trading Oluwaseun Adebayo-Clarke at a London brokerage has built an automated system that now handles most of her desk's routine trades. Marcus, a trader of twenty years, has just learned that his job is likely to be cut and has begun sharing his own strategies with a rival firm in a bid to secure a position there. She may be able to prevent this by cutting his access immediately, but that would effectively signal dismissal before the formal consultation process the firm owes him. She must act before the market opens in the morning.
options: Restrict Marcus's access to sensitive strategy files immediately, explain why in writing and proceed with consultation.
Leave his access intact until the consultation concludes, accepting the risk of leaked strategies as the cost of fair process.
Offer him a transparent early exit package conditional on handing over his strategy knowledge and signing a confidentiality agreement.
tension: protecting company assets vs. fair treatment

title: Automated sorting at the postal depot in Lusaka
scenario: Depot manager Chilufya Mulenga oversees forty sorters who read handwritten addresses and route parcels across Zambia. The national postal service has funded an optical sorting machine that would handle most of the volume with fewer errors. Sorters know local place names, nicknames for villages and informal landmarks that the machine cannot read, and rural parcels are often addressed that way. Retaining only a dozen sorters would save money, but rural deliveries might fail more often. The ministry expects a staffing plan for the installation by next Friday.
options: Install the machine and keep a dozen of the best sorters to handle unreadable rural addresses, offering the others retraining or severance.
Install the machine but retain all sorters for a year, redeploying them to handle exceptions while the machine learns local addresses.
Postpone installation until the machine can be adapted to local address conventions, accepting delay and loss of the funding offer.
